title: Chicken or turkey with cheese sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken and turkey are lean sources of protein that are often served with a rich cheese sauce. The dish combines juicy poultry meat with a creamy sauce made from cheese, milk, and spices, making it a favorite in both home cooking and restaurant menus.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese sauce can be made from various cheeses: cheddar, mozzarella, parmesan, or processed cheese.
In the United States the dish is often baked, while in Europe it is commonly served as a piece of meat topped with sauce.
Turkey contains slightly less fat than chicken, but both birds are rich in B‑vitamins.
Cheese sauces are frequently enhanced with mustard or paprika for extra flavor.
The dish cooks quickly: the meat is sautéed and the sauce is simmered for a few minutes.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is a good source of niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The cheese sauce adds calcium, important for bone and dental health.

items.title: Low saturated fat (when using low‑fat cheese)
items.content: Choosing reduced‑fat cheese varieties can keep saturated fat levels modest.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: The sauce often contributes phosphorus and zinc, which aid immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese sauce may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy allergies.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheeses can be high in salt; monitor added salt during preparation.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The creamy sauce increases the dish’s calories, so serve in moderate portions.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Poultry must be fully cooked to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically with a side of potatoes, rice, or vegetables. Slice the meat, coat it with cheese sauce, and optionally bake until golden. Garnish with fresh herbs or spices for added aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly until bubbling. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months if portioned beforehand.
